title: Meet the employer's general health and safety duty
what: Provide and maintain, so far as is reasonably practicable, a working environment that is safe and without risks to health.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: s 21(1) (authorised version 045, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: (1) An employer must, so far as is reasonably practicable, provide and maintain for employees of the employer a working environment that is safe and without risks to health.

sources.title: Summary of the OHS Act 2004: General OHS Duties
sources.locator: Duties of employers to employees and contractors (section 21)
sources.quote: The OHS Act requires all employers to provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risks to health. This duty is to be met so far as is reasonably practicable.

confidence_note: Quoted from the authorised PDF the owner saved from the Victorian register (data/raw/vic_legislation/, not committed); the register's documents disallow automated fetching. The regulator's guidance quoted before is kept as a second source.

assessment.summary: Every business must ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health and safety of its workers and others affected by its work.

marks.reason: Safety systems, consultation and records that every business must keep up.
A different safety law in the second-largest state raises the cost of operating nationally.
